experiment: Covering index on isolated copy; no production or builder change.
method: Alternating variant order by repetition. Each timed sample uses a fresh Python process and fresh Engine, measures its first lookup after initialization, then 50 exact-same-query snapshot hits separately. Initialization scans the dictionary; OS filesystem cache is uncontrolled. These are application-cache-cold queries, not cold disk or changing-keystroke/native end-to-end timings. Traced memory runs are separate and their elapsed times are excluded from timing summaries.
memory_method: Windows working-set/private-byte snapshots inspect only each benchmark process. Tracemalloc measures incremental Python allocation after Engine initialization and omits native SQLite/C allocations. Process peak working set includes startup and is not a query-only peak.

post_run_full_snapshot_verification.method: Separate untimed fresh Engine per variant and query, compares every retained ranked candidate with score, reading, match_type and consumed_input, plus completion-truncation flag. Same production/database/module fingerprints checked before and after. Does not assert exhaustive completion coverage beyond the bounded engine pools.

interpretation.recommendation: Material application-cache-cold query improvement supports a separately tested and reproducible builder index change; this experiment does not modify production or establish native responsiveness.
interpretation.mechanism: SQLite chooses the added covering index, eliminating table payload lookups for these reads. Prefix ranges still require a temporary B-tree for global weight ordering; exact-base equality avoids that sort.
limits: Five first-query samples per variant/query cannot characterize rare stalls or tail latency.
Initialization remains roughly two seconds and is outside first-lookup timing.
Filesystem cache and concurrent machine workload are uncontrolled.
Exact-same-query warm samples only test the snapshot cache, not changing keystrokes.
Broad s and toned lei4 indexed medians remain above the future 20ms warm-query goal.
Tracemalloc omits native SQLite allocations; working-set snapshots are not query-only peak measurements.
